chronology: Recap: Othon Von Salza marries Edna (daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka) on Marmola; they have son Bari; Berard passes the family legacy to Othon before dying.

The Castaka clan's secret anti-gravity oil Epyphite is exposed to the Imperial Merchants Guild during a crisis; a fleet battle erupts over Marmola; the black endoguards defect from the Empire and win.
Othon breaks Bari's legs to stop him fighting; Edna goes alone to confront the invaders to defend clan honor and is disintegrated at the base of a great column.
An armored speaker publicly denounces imperial generals as treacherous before the guards; the guards open fire.
Othon organizes a three-pronged counterattack: Hohenhole attacks north, Konrath attacks south via secret tunnels, Othon infiltrates the enemy center alone with only a short dagger.
Othon kills approximately 1,500 endoguards by exploiting tiny gaps in their supposedly impenetrable armor — a feat later recounted as a legendary ancestral exploit to Tonto.
In the aftermath Othon searches the northern battlefield for Hohenhole, carries Konrath's body south through the ruins, and mourns Edna at the column where she was disintegrated.
Oda falls in battle; Bari, wounded and bedridden, condemns his father as a coward then breaks down and asks forgiveness; father and son reconcile.
News of Othon's deeds spreads galaxy-wide via interstellar spies; Othon is recognized as the new Baron of Castaka.
One week later the imperial couple arrives at Marmola in their golden vessel with a purple Endoguard; Othon and Bari are publicly honored.
In private negotiations Othon uses exclusive knowledge of the Epyphite's location as leverage; he warns that coercion alone would take years and demands terms.

Othon secures a revenue share from Epyphite sales (founding the Metabarons' great fortune) and inherits the world of Okhar in the Diamond Constellation, where the Castaka fortress is rebuilt stone by stone.
As an additional gift for Bari, Othon obtains Shazam — a white horse from a breed extinct for 20,000 years, recreated by imperial techno-scientists at a cost of 100 tons of gold.
On Okhar Bari bonds with Shazam and enters a happier phase of life; Othon, now Master Othon, confides loneliness to attendant Iku-Tta.
An armed raiding party (Ulkran, Wulthor, Tokkar, Bargoth) uses a paleo-compass and a marble disintegrator to breach the fortress on Okhar and steals Shazam using synthetic mare essence.
Bari pursues the thieves despite his crippled legs; Othon is alerted by a servant, suppresses a public alarm to protect Bari's honor, and dons his own armor.
Othon ambushes the raiders in dense fog exploiting terrain knowledge and a bow; Bari also fights the green-skinned raiders; Othon suffers catastrophic injury to his groin and hips.
Shazam carries the gravely wounded Othon back to his palace; Iku-Tta and his two daughters nurse Othon through months of delirious recovery.
Recovering, Othon invests his fortune in developing the first metabaronic weapons and begins the lineage tradition of cybernetic implants, including a multi-protonic pelvis.
Despite his castration, Othon fathers a biological son, Bari Didi, ensuring direct blood succession.
Volume closes with a teaser for the next episode: the knighting of Othon.
locations: Marmola — the marble planet, homeworld of the Castaka clan, site of the Epyphite reservoir and the fleet battle.
Castaka domain on Marmola — the family's stronghold and quarrying territory.
Space above Marmola — site of the fleet battle between the Empire and the black endoguards.
Epyphite reservoir — a vast subterranean cavern beneath Marmola, accessed via a passage carved by the Castakas thousands of years ago; described as a luminous, ocean-like expanse.
Valley battlefield on Marmola — post-battle aftermath zone where Othon searches for Hohenhole and retrieves Konrath's body.
Okhar — a fertile planet in the Diamond Constellation granted to Othon by the Empire; the Castaka fortress was transferred and rebuilt there.
Marble fortress on Okhar — the relocated Castaka stronghold; breached by raiders using a paleo-compass and marble disintegrator.
Golden imperial vessel — the distinctive ship used by the imperial couple to travel to Marmola for negotiations.
Framing narrative setting — an unspecified interior where a small floating narrator recounts Othon's history to Tonto and Lothar.
lore_laws: Epyphite is a sacred anti-gravity oil found deep beneath Marmola, described as the planet's sacred blood; the Castakas revered and guarded it for thousands of years before its exposure to the Empire.
Endoguards are a military force with allegedly impenetrable armor; their only vulnerability is tiny gaps between plates, exploitable with precise close-range dagger strikes.
The black endoguards defected from the Empire during the Marmola battle and fought on the Castaka side.

Horses have been extinct for 20,000 years since the Sixth World War; the Imperial Palace maintains a genetic museum from which extinct species can be recreated by techno-scientists — Shazam cost 100 tons of gold.
A paleo-compass can locate marble structures at range; a marble disintegrator can breach marble barriers.
Synthetic mare essence, reproduced by technologists, can calm and guide a horse even after millennia of extinction.

Othon Von Salza founded two defining traditions of the Metabaron lineage: development of specialized metabaronic weapons and the practice of cybernetic body augmentation, exemplified by his multi-protonic pelvis.
The passage to the Epyphite reservoir beneath Marmola was carved by the Castakas thousands of years ago.
The Metabarons' immense fortune originates from a negotiated percentage of Epyphite sale proceeds granted by the Empire.
Warrior doctrine attributed to 'the Baron' holds that true valor transcends both triumph and defeat, and that tactical deception is acceptable in service of victory.
major_events: Battle of Marmola: the black endoguards defect from the Empire and win the fleet battle over control of the Epyphite.
Edna's death: she confronts the invading force alone to defend clan honor and is disintegrated at the base of a column.
Othon's solo infiltration: armed with only a short dagger, Othon kills approximately 1,500 endoguards by exploiting tiny gaps in their armor, becoming a founding legend of the Metabaron lineage.
Post-battle mourning and reconciliation: Othon recovers Konrath's body, honors Edna's death site, and reconciles with a remorseful Bari over Oda's funeral bier.
Empire-Castaka negotiations: Othon leverages exclusive knowledge of the Epyphite to extract a revenue share, the planet Okhar, and the gift of Shazam for Bari.
Theft of Shazam: an armed raiding party breaches the marble fortress on Okhar and steals the resurrected horse using synthetic mare essence.
Othon's castration: hunting the raiders in fog, Othon defeats them but suffers catastrophic groin and hip injuries; Shazam carries him home.
Founding of the metabaronic tradition: Othon creates the first metabaronic weapons and initiates the family practice of cybernetic body augmentation.
Succession confirmed: despite castration, Othon fathers biological heir Bari Didi, preserving the bloodline.
open_uncertainties: Hohenhole's ultimate fate after the battle is not confirmed; Othon searches for him in the northern battlefield but no resolution is shown within the volume.
The exact identities of the two unnamed figures speaking in the imperial context (p09 top panel) are not stated on the page.
Whether the raiding party that stole Shazam acted independently or at someone's behest is never established.
The nature of the green-skinned raiders — distinct species, augmented humans, or fighters with unusual coloring — is not explained.
The method by which the castrated Othon fathered Bari Didi biologically is raised as a question by Lothar but the explanation is cut off before completion.
The printed page numbers visible in several scans do not match the supplied page labels, suggesting a possible discrepancy between issue-internal numbering and the file sequence.
The exact identity and nature of the small floating narrator who addresses Tonto are not stated on any page.
recurring_motifs: Father-son conflict, physical punishment, and reconciliation: Othon breaks Bari's legs; Bari condemns then forgives his father; Othon suppresses alarm to shield Bari's reputation.
Physical mutilation as dynastic turning point: Bari's broken legs and Othon's castration each reshape the lineage's future.
Honor versus pragmatism: characters openly contest whether glorious death, tactical deception, or survival best fulfills the warrior code.
Tribute to the fallen: Othon personally retrieves Konrath's body and mourns at Edna's death site, framing loyalty to the dead as sacred duty.
Ancestral exploit as oral legend: Othon's dagger feat is retold in the framing narrative to Tonto, establishing the series' storytelling frame.
Restoration of the extinct at extreme cost: Shazam the resurrected horse and Othon's cybernetic pelvis both represent enormous expenditure to recover what was destroyed.
Secrecy as power: the Epyphite secret, Bari's shame, and the fogbound raid all hinge on controlling what others know.
title: The Last Stand
